```{r setup, include=FALSE}
stopifnot(packageVersion("dsOMOPClient") == "2.10.5")
library(dsOMOPClient)
stopifnot(!is.null(params$conns),length(params$conns)>=2L)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(error=FALSE,warning=FALSE,message=FALSE)
source(system.file("examples","audit-numeric-studies.R",package="dsOMOPClient"))
```

This lesson requires the integrated 2.10.5 pair. These constructors are not
2.10.4 APIs. The acceptance fixture is synthetic: each person has values 3, 3,
9 on January 1 and 15 on January 2, in one declared numeric unit. It is not a
GiBleed laboratory dataset or a clinical reference range. GiBleed is suitable
for basic OMOP structure; numeric laboratory lessons need the versioned
Synthea27Nj fixture or an explicitly labelled synthetic fixture such as this.

Selection, calendar-day weighting and final presentation
------------------------------------------------------

The event's unit policy is explicit. Each day contributes once after its
within-day mean. Days without observations do not appear. Multiple episodes
still belong to their real people; they do not increase disclosure support.

```{r daily-declaration}
lab <- omop_event("measurement",3000963L,name="lab",unit=omop_unit(8554L))
raw <- omop_variable(event=lab,reducer=omop_reduce("mean"))
daily <- omop_number_daily(omop_number_rows(lab),omop_reduce("mean"))
study <- omop_recipe(variables=list(raw=raw,daily=daily),
  populations=omop_population("p",index=omop_index(lab)),
  outputs=omop_output("o",rows="p"))
result <- recipe_execute(study,out="AuditLesson",symbol=params$resource,
                         conns=params$conns,output_mode="memory")
```

Only admitted aggregates are displayed. The independent hand answers are raw
record mean 7.5 and mean of daily means 10. `ds.quantileMean` combines site
quantiles; it does not generally compute exact pooled quantiles.

```{r admitted-aggregates}
raw_mean <- dsBaseClient::ds.mean("AuditLesson$raw",type="combine",datasources=params$conns)
day_mean <- dsBaseClient::ds.mean("AuditLesson$daily",type="combine",datasources=params$conns)
stopifnot(abs(raw_mean$Global.Mean[1,1]-7.5)<1e-10,
          abs(day_mean$Global.Mean[1,1]-10)<1e-10)
print(raw_mean)
print(day_mean)
day_quantiles <- dsBaseClient::ds.quantileMean("AuditLesson$daily",type="combine",datasources=params$conns)
stopifnot(all(abs(unlist(day_quantiles)[1:7]-10)<1e-10))
print(day_quantiles)
```

Staging uses the same final gate and declared meaning. A staged descriptor is
not a generic R data frame; consumer compatibility requires its supported
restoration adapter. This chunk validates the published metadata, without
claiming a direct dsBase call on a descriptor.

```{r staged-publication}
staged <- recipe_execute(study,out="AuditLessonStaged",symbol=params$resource,
                         conns=params$conns,output_mode="staged")
books <- recipe_codebook(staged)
stopifnot(length(books)==1L,books[[1]]$status=="published")
print(books[[1]]$columns[,c("name","semantic_type","unit","privacy_class")])
```

Exercises with executable declarations
-------------------------------------

The supplied study declarations use the existing closed numeric operations.
The server acceptance file `test-audit-study-recipes.R` executes their independent
oracles through the normal final gate. The following chunks rebuild each public
declaration; they do not print patient rows.

```{r study-declarations}
windows <- audit_windows()
pre_index <- audit_windows(TRUE)
comparisons <- audit_numeric_studies(lab)
stopifnot(all(c("difference","ratio","percent_change","observation_fraction",
               "previous_days_min","current_day_max","clean_mean") %in% names(comparisons)))
length(comparisons)
```

1. Occurrence starts at offsets -366, -365, -181, -180, -31, -30, 0, 1 give
   6/4/2 for the inclusive long/medium/short windows and 5/3/1 for pre-index
   windows. Era-overlap selection is a different question. FE catalogue zero
   means all-history cohort-member prevalence, not these windows.
2. Independently selected baseline and six-month visits are not contemporaneous.
   Baseline 10/follow-up 15 gives difference 5, ratio 1.5 and percentage change
   50; follow-up 20 at another site's visit schedule gives 10, 2 and 100.
3. Values 4, 6, 10, NA give eligible-observation fraction 2/3 in inclusive [4,6]
   and one value above 6. This is not glucose elapsed time in range.
4. Previous-calendar-days minimum [-7,-1] and current-day maximum [0,0] are
   episode-scoped day summaries. Same-day candidates are excluded from history;
   two recorded dates do not establish a 48-hour interval. Count distinct people,
   not episodes or inferred incident AKI events.
5. Heights 170/400 with declared bounds [0,250] give raw mean 285, pre-reduction
   set-NA mean 170 and clipped mean 210. Cleaning the already-reduced mean is
   different. Bounds here are synthetic teaching declarations.
6. Check integer equality before ordinal pain bins: 0/10 valid, 2.5/11 invalid,
   missing remains missing. Keep all declared levels 0 through 10, including
   unused levels, with an explicit model contrast/reference.

```{r pain-declaration}
pain <- audit_pain_scale(omop_variable(event=lab,reducer=omop_reduce("last_value")))
stopifnot(setequal(names(pain),c("numeric","ordinal")))
```

Formula inputs and units
------------------------

BMI uses kg/metres; MAP is the arithmetic approximation (SBP + 2 DBP)/3, not
measured arterial pressure. eGFR uses the race-free CKD-EPI 2021 creatinine
formula, explicit IDMS-standardized mg/dL, completed calendar years at the
selected creatinine measurement, adult eligibility and explicit disjoint sex
mapping. Unknown sex, age under 18 and invalid creatinine produce missing.
A declared conversion of 88.4 µmol/L per mg/dL belongs before the formula.
No formula infers units, assay suitability or sex from an observed value.

```{r formula-declaration}
weight <- omop_number(raw,omop_number_spec(unit=omop_number_unit("unit:8554","coordinate:kg",1)))
height <- omop_number(raw,omop_number_spec(unit=omop_number_unit("unit:8554","coordinate:metres",1)))
bmi <- omop_formula_bmi(weight,height)
stopifnot(inherits(bmi,"omop_variable"))
```

The teaching declaration above illustrates explicit coordinates; the same raw
column must not be treated as actual weight and height in a real study. The
formula acceptance uses separate, known synthetic 80 kg and 2 m operands and
checks BMI 20 against an independent oracle.

Pooling, meaning and reproducibility
-----------------------------------

A pooled sufficient-statistic mean weights sites by eligible people. A mean of
site estimates answers a different question. Withheld is never zero.

```{r pooling-exercise}
site_n <- c(2,8); site_mean <- c(10,20)
stopifnot(weighted.mean(site_mean,site_n)==18,mean(site_mean)==15)
data.frame(pooled_mean=weighted.mean(site_mean,site_n),mean_of_site_means=mean(site_mean))
```

A pooled GLM is not inverse-variance SLMA. Personal rates, episode-days and
unioned person-days have different denominators. Repeated rows require a
within-person dependence model. A person-period Poisson GLM must declare the
count outcome, log link, log(person-time) offset and dependence assumptions;
SCCS partitions alone are preparation, not a conditional SCCS estimate.
Cross-site resource checks do not deduplicate someone attending two hospitals.

Equal labels do not establish equivalent instruments, question universes,
coverage or vocabulary expansion. Compare codebooks, full source definitions,
unit conversions, missing/unavailable policies and reference versions. Retain
namespace, scope digest and definition when joining covariate IDs.

```{r local-bundle}
bundle <- recipe_study_bundle(result,list(id="audit-day-weighting",protocol_version="1.0.0",
  roles=list(target=list(population="p")),reference_versions=list(fixture="synthetic-day-values-1")))
stopifnot(bundle$snapshot$status=="unknown")
print(bundle$publication$status)
```

A plan digest identifies a declaration, not a database snapshot. Supply an
already-authorized owner snapshot ID and provenance if available. Bundle
construction makes no network calls and cannot certify equal data between runs
or a complete Strategus study.

Migration appendix and disclosure boundary
------------------------------------------

Keep historical v1 recipes in the compatibility layer. New work uses native
language 2 and its typed declarations. Use integer JSON concept IDs and Boolean
flags. An unsupported Circe clause refuses instead of weakening a phenotype.
If a clinically required clean period or feature window is unsupported by a
catalogue route, use an explicitly validated native recipe; dropping the
scientific requirement is not an equivalent migration.

Private computation may contain small groups. Final accessible components are
gated on distinct people; protected aggregates apply their own declared
contract. No raw-row workaround, privacy budget, per-user answer policy or
mandatory database TLS is introduced. Deterministic noise does not guarantee
lifetime composition privacy under adaptive queries or evolving data. Shared
roots preserve identity/noise continuity only when the deployment retains them.
